proposals.hypothesis: Li2SiF6 is a Li-rich fluorosilicate with Si4+ in a closed-shell, very hard-to-reduce center bonded to F. Fluoride frameworks with closed-shell cations (Li3AlF6, LiMgAlF6, LiCaAlF6, Li2ZrF6) have given the lowest contact penalties so far, while oxide, phosphate, borate and silicate coatings gave 0.29 to 0.77 eV/non-Li atom. Si4+ should resist reduction by the sulfide/chloride electrolyte and form strong Si-F bonds, so this should stay in the low-penalty fluoride regime.
proposals.motivation: LiCaAlF6 (mp-aaaaajby) was acceptable at 0.048 eV/non-Li atom (bin 2). Li2ZrF6 (mp-aaaaafxy) gave 0.099 (bin 4), and the fluoride family consistently outperformed the other families. Li2SiF6 is a different fluoride cation, so it tests whether the Si-F framework does as well as the Zr and Al fluorides.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5-6 eV) insulating phosphate that is oxidatively stable up to about 4 V vs Li and is a well-known protective coating for LiCoO2. Its phosphate chemistry should limit interfacial reactions with the sulfide electrolyte, which makes it a strong first candidate for a low-penalty interface.

LiNbO3 is the benchmark sulfide-compatible oxide coating for LiCoO2. It is wide-gap and insulating, with a high-valent Nb5+ d0 center that should be more reduction-tolerant against the sulfide/chloride electrolyte than the phosphate. This is a different family from the Li3PO4 that gave a 0.34 eV/atom penalty from P-S/Cl-driven decomposition.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaauhx) was evaluated; its penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom (bin 16) came from contact decomposition to P2O5, SCl4 and SO2, so the coating's reactivity with the sulfide is the limiting factor and a different oxide chemistry is worth testing.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a wide-gap, highly insulating, Li-rich halide with a very low tendency to be reduced by sulfide or chloride electrolytes. Its fluoride anion is also oxidatively robust against LiCoO2 at 4 V. Both prior oxide and phosphate coatings produced contact decomposition penalties (~0.29-0.34 eV/atom), so a halide with no reducible non-Li cation should give a lower penalty.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaauhx) and LiNbO3 (mp-aaaaafnn) both gave penalties above 0.29 eV/non-Li atom from P/S/Cl-driven contact decomposition, so the oxide and phosphate families appear reactive against the sulfide electrolyte.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a fully lithiated orthoborate with a wide gap and B3+ in a closed-shell, hard-to-reduce environment. Unlike the phosphate, oxide, and fluoride coatings already tested, it has no P-S or P-Cl exchange pathway and no reducible high-valent d-metal, so it may avoid the contact decomposition seen at 0.29-0.34 eV/atom.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4, LiNbO3, and LiF all gave contact penalties of 0.29-0.34 eV/non-Li atom, none acceptable, from reactions with the sulfide/chloride electrolyte. A borate family has not been tried yet.

proposal.hypothesis: Li4SiO4 is a fully lithiated, wide-gap orthosilicate with Si4+ in a closed-shell tetrahedral site that is very hard to reduce. The silicate family has not been tested yet.
